findings.title: Carried over and deferred by agreement: sanitizeGroupTitle still does not strip Unicode Cc/Cf code points
findings.description: Restated on the final state for the record; not re-litigated, and I do not disagree with the deferral. src/data/migration.ts:45 still reads `value.trim().slice(0, GROUP_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH).replace(/[\uD800-\uDBFF]$/, '')`, and String.prototype.trim() removes ECMAScript WhiteSpace/LineTerminator only, not category Cc/Cf. Consequences unchanged: a bidi override (U+202E) in a stored group title reorders the header line around the name, and a title composed only of zero-width characters (U+200B, U+FEFF) survives trim(), so it reads as 'renamed' to both resolveGroupTitle() (src/ui/groupTitle.ts:10) and the EmptyState hint check (src/ui/EmptyState.svelte:11) while rendering visually blank — a blank-looking header plus a silently switched hint. Confirmed again at HEAD that migration.ts is untouched by all three Task 06 commits; it belongs to Task 03. The disposition is now recorded in the decisions log under Task 06 → Tech debt with the fix location and owner named explicitly ('лечить — в `updateBoard` задачи 08 плюс тот же класс символов в санитайзере'), which is what I asked for. Deferral accepted.
findings.location: src/data/migration.ts:45 (sanitizeGroupTitle); surfaced at src/ui/GroupHeader.svelte:19, src/ui/CollapsibleGroup.svelte:42, src/ui/GroupSettingsPopup.svelte:30
findings.impact: Visual misrepresentation of board chrome only. No script execution, no data access, no privilege change, no persistence beyond what the user already controls. Requires a hand-edited or externally supplied data.json — plausible via Obsidian Sync or a git-backed vault, which is why it is recorded rather than dismissed.
findings.recommendation: No action in Task 06 — this requires no change to any file this task owns and must not block it. In Task 08, strip before trimming so a zero-width-only title collapses to '' and falls back to the localized default: `return value.replace(/[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}]/gu, '').trim().slice(0, GROUP_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH).replace(/[\uD800-\uDBFF]$/, '');`

findings.category: A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
findings.title: Process control gap that produced the round-2 critical is understood and recorded, but nothing yet prevents recurrence in Tasks 09 and 10
findings.description: Downgraded from the round-2 critical, which is resolved — this is the residual systemic issue, not the incident. Root cause, now established: three reviewer agents audited one shared working tree concurrently and two of them ran in-place source mutations; one mutant (src/ui/GroupSettingsPopup.svelte, and, per the evidence in finding-2-retracted below, a GroupHeader mutant as well) was still on disk when I measured gates against the tree rather than against a commit. That single fact manufactured one false critical and one false minor in my round-2 report. The recurrence risk is concrete, not hypothetical: the decisions log hands Tasks 09 and 10 explicit mutation-testing follow-ups ('после миграции стоит прогнать мутант D ещё раз', 'выживший мутант C'), i.e. the same shared-tree mutation pattern is scheduled to run again. The org conclusion is already written down in the decisions log ('мутационная проверка, которая правит исходники на месте, обязана снимать мутанта тем же действием, а цифру гейта в отчёте нужно привязывать к коммиту, а не к дереву'), which is the right rule; what does not exist is any mechanism that enforces it. I followed it myself in this round: my own canary experiment ran in a throwaway `git worktree` at a4fda4e, never in the user's tree, and the worktree was removed and pruned in the same breath (`git worktree list` now shows only the main checkout).
findings.location: Process — reviewer orchestration for feature 0011; recorded in 0011-feat-group-customization-decisions.md, Task 06 → Reviews
findings.impact: No impact on the shipped artifact. The cost is review integrity: a gate figure measured against a mutable shared tree is not attributable to any commit, and in round 2 that cost the pipeline a full extra review round on two findings that were both measurement artifacts. If it recurs in Task 09 or 10 the same waste repeats, and the worse failure mode is the inverse — a mutant that makes a gate pass and is quoted as evidence.
findings.recommendation: Two cheap rules, both already implied by the decisions-log conclusion: (1) any agent that mutates source in place does so in a throwaway `git worktree add --detach <sha>` rather than the shared tree, and removes it in the same step; (2) every gate figure quoted in a review report names the SHA it was measured against, and the report states whether `git diff HEAD --stat -- src/ tests/` was empty at measurement time. Optionally, have the orchestrator run `git status --short` between reviewer waves so divergence is caught by the pipeline rather than by the next reviewer.

roundTwoFindingsResolved.roundTwoFinding: MINOR — 'Task 06 introduced a new Svelte build warning (GroupHeader has unused export property groupId)' (best-practice)
roundTwoFindingsResolved.verification: The finding was wrong and I withdraw it. Measurement on the clean tree: `npm run build` at a4fda4e emits exactly 2 warnings, both the pre-existing a11y notices on BoardSettingsPopup.svelte:31 and GroupSettingsPopup.svelte:29. There is no `unused export property 'groupId'` warning. The same 2-warning figure appears independently in the Playwright webServer build log during the 84/84 run. I then settled attribution positively rather than merely observing the absence, in a throwaway worktree detached at a4fda4e (never in the user's tree): baseline build → 2 warnings; then applying the GroupHeader canary mutant (`$: title = resolveGroupTitle(...)` → `$: title = group.title ?? '';`) → 3 warnings, the third being verbatim `GroupHeader has unused export property 'groupId'`. So the mutant is both necessary and sufficient to produce the warning I reported, and dev-code-reviewer's prediction was exactly right: dropping the resolveGroupTitle call orphans the groupId prop, because Svelte 4's unused-export-let heuristic stops counting a prop read only inside a removed reactive declaration. Task 06 introduced no build warning. Where my round-2 method broke: I compared a build in a *clean worktree* at dc34591 against a build in the *dirty shared tree* at HEAD and attributed the delta to the diff between the commits. The delta was the mutant. The worktree was removed and pruned immediately after the experiment (`git worktree list` shows only the main checkout; `rm -f` on the symlinked node_modules first, so nothing outside the scratchpad was touched). By extension, my round-1 'only pre-existing a11y warnings' claim was correct after all and stands uncorrected.

verifiedClean: Working-tree integrity — the round-2 blocker. `git diff HEAD --stat -- src/ tests/` empty; `git status --short` shows only untracked review JSONs, the pre-existing untracked logs/ directory, and the two orchestrator-owned docs files described in auditTarget. No stray spec files: tests/e2e/ contains exactly its five tracked files and a repo-wide find for zz-tmp*/tmp-debug* returns nothing.
Build gate on the clean tree: `npm run build` succeeds with 2 warnings, both pre-existing a11y notices. This is the same count as before Task 06 and settles round-2 finding 2 in the task's favour.

Test gates, both reproduced by me this round, both against a tree provably equal to a4fda4e: `npx playwright test` → 84 passed / 0 failed (25.0s); `npm test` (vitest 4.0.18) → 84 passed across 6 files. The vitest gate that I could not reproduce in round 2 is now confirmed rather than trusted — the ERR_REQUIRE_ESM was purely the Node version (default v18.19.1 against declared engines ^22.12.0 || >=24.0.0); running under /snap/bin (v22.23.1) collects and passes cleanly. My round-2 note that this was an environment limitation on my side, not a code defect, is confirmed.

XSS posture of the six touched files: unchanged from round 2 and re-verified on the final state. Repo-wide grep for {@html, innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval(, new Function across src/ yields exactly one hit — the prose warning in the src/ui/groupTitle.ts docblock. All three sites that render a group name are Svelte {} text interpolations, which the compiler escapes: GroupHeader.svelte:19, CollapsibleGroup.svelte:42, GroupSettingsPopup.svelte:30.

Value-flow trace re-run at HEAD: every consumer of the name (group.title / groupTitle / storedTitle / resolveGroupTitle) is accounted for — five components plus the resolver, the sanitizer call site at migration.ts:157, and the unit test. Not one routes the name into an attribute, style binding, tooltip, URL or data-* value. Every title= attribute in the touched components carries an i18n key ($t('groupHeader.settings'), $t('groupHeader.addTask')); style bindings are numeric only (--tm-card-columns: {columns}); data-group-id={groupId} is a fixed GroupId union member.
src/ui/groupTitle.ts still exports exactly one function and remains untouched by all three Task 06 commits, per Task 05's constraint.

Commit a4fda4e is test-only, as described: `git show --stat` is `tests/e2e/core.spec.ts | 5 +++++`, a single toHaveText('Backlog') assertion added inside existing test 7.1 on a class-based locator. No source file, harness or fixture changed; no new test scenario; no credentials, secrets, network endpoints or dependencies. Zero security surface.

No hardcoded secrets in the Task 06 diff: grep over `git diff dc34591..HEAD` for api key / secret / password / token / private-key / bearer / authorization patterns returns nothing. No dependency or build-config change either — package.json, package-lock.json, manifest.json, esbuild.config.mjs, playwright.config.ts and vitest.config.ts are all untouched across dc34591..HEAD, so A06 (vulnerable components) and A08 (supply chain) have no new exposure from this task.

The untracked logs/ directory was inspected since it is not in .gitignore and could therefore be committed by accident: it holds two review JSONs from the earlier 0003 green-border feature (16K total), containing review prose only — no credentials, no PII, no vault contents. Pre-existing and unrelated to Task 06; noted, not a finding.

My own footprint in this audit: one throwaway git worktree under the scratchpad, detached at a4fda4e, used for the warning-attribution canary, removed and pruned in the same step. No mutation, file or process of mine remains in the user's tree — `git worktree list` shows only the main checkout and `git diff HEAD -- src/ tests/` is empty after all my work.
